title: New Scientific Discovery Offers Hope for Fertility Challenges
subtitle: Researchers have created a way to stabilize chromosomes in aging eggs, potentially changing the future of IVF treatments.

summary.en: Many people are choosing to have children later in life, but this often leads to biological difficulties. A new study from the Max Planck Institute has found a way to support chromosomes in aging eggs. By using a new protein system, scientists successfully stabilized these structures in mouse eggs. This discovery could eventually help improve the success rates of in-vitro fertilization. Experts believe this work is a significant step forward in understanding and preventing pregnancy loss.
summary.zh: 許多人選擇在較晚的年齡生育，但這往往會導致生理上的困難。馬克斯普朗克研究所的一項新研究發現了一種支撐高齡卵子中染色體的方法。透過使用一種新的蛋白質系統，科學家成功穩定了小鼠卵子中的這些結構。這項發現最終可能有助於提高人工受孕的成功率。專家認為，這項工作在理解與預防妊娠流失方面邁出了重要的一步。

paragraphs.en: Across the globe, more people are deciding to start families later in their lives for many social and economic reasons. However, as people get older, they often face a difficult biological challenge. A major cause of infertility and failed in-vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles—a process where an egg is fertilized by sperm outside the body—is a problem called aneuploidy. This happens when chromosomes, which carry our genetic information, fail to separate correctly during cell division. According to STAT News, this issue becomes much more common after the age of 40, with studies showing that between 50% and 80% of embryos from women in their 40s have these chromosomal errors.
paragraphs.zh: 全球各地有越來越多人基於許多社會與經濟因素，決定在人生較晚的階段才開始建立家庭。然而，隨著年齡增長，人們往往面臨艱鉅的生理挑戰。導致不孕以及人工受孕（IVF，即在體外將卵子與精子結合的過程）失敗的主要原因之一，是一種稱為「非整倍體」的問題。當攜帶遺傳資訊的染色體在細胞分裂過程中無法正確分離時，就會發生這種情況。根據 STAT 新聞報導，這個問題在四十歲後變得非常普遍，研究顯示四十多歲女性的胚胎中，有百分之五十到八十存在這些染色體異常。

paragraphs.en: To understand why this happens, it is important to look at how cells work. When a cell prepares to divide, chromosomes form copies called sister chromatids. These are held together by a protein complex known as cohesin. You can think of cohesin as a kind of "molecular glue" that keeps the chromosomes connected until they are ready to separate. In most parts of the body, this glue only needs to work for a few hours. However, in female egg cells, or oocytes, this bond must last for decades. Female babies are born with all the egg cells they will ever have, and these cells must hold their genetic material together until fertilization happens years or even decades later. Over time, this glue does not get replaced, which leads to the errors that cause infertility and miscarriage.
paragraphs.zh: 要了解為何會發生這種情況，必須先觀察細胞的運作方式。當細胞準備分裂時，染色體會形成稱為「姊妹染色分體」的複製品。這些複製品由一種稱為「黏連蛋白」的蛋白質複合體緊密結合在一起。你可以將黏連蛋白想像成一種「分子膠水」，在染色體準備好分離前，將它們連接在一起。在人體大多數部位，這種膠水只需要運作幾個小時；然而在女性卵細胞（即卵母細胞）中，這種連結必須維持數十年之久。女嬰出生時就擁有了她一生中所有的卵細胞，而這些細胞必須將遺傳物質緊緊結合，直到多年甚至數十年後受精發生為止。隨著時間推移，這種膠水無法被替換，進而導致了造成不孕與流產的錯誤。

paragraphs.en: Recently, researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Germany have made a breakthrough in this area. Led by Melina Schuh, the team spent eight years developing a new protein system to fix this problem. As reported by STAT News, the researchers created a system called TALhesins. These engineered proteins are designed to attach to chromosomes and act as a replacement for the lost natural glue. In their study, which was published in the journal Science, the team successfully restored normal chromosome connections in aging mouse eggs.
paragraphs.zh: 近期，德國馬克斯普朗克多學科科學研究所（Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences）的研究人員在此領域取得了突破。在梅琳娜·舒（Melina Schuh）的帶領下，該團隊耗時八年開發出一套新的蛋白質系統來解決此問題。正如 STAT 新聞所報導，研究人員創造了一種稱為「TALhesins」的系統。這些工程蛋白質旨在附著於染色體上，作為遺傳物質流失後的天然膠水替代品。在發表於《科學》（Science）期刊的研究中，該團隊成功恢復了高齡小鼠卵子中正常的染色體連結。

paragraphs.en: This research is being watched closely by experts in the field. Rajiv McCoy, a biologist at Johns Hopkins University, noted that while there is still much work to be done, the team’s proof of concept—a demonstration that a new idea can actually work in practice—was highly successful. McCoy, whose own research focuses on pregnancy loss, explained that aneuploidy is the leading cause of why pregnancies end before birth. He stated that technologies capable of reducing these errors could have a massive impact on the IVF industry and society as a whole. Because about half of all human conceptions are lost before birth, any method that can help stabilize these cells could change the lives of many families.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究正受到該領域專家的密切關注。約翰霍普金斯大學（Johns Hopkins University）的生物學家拉吉夫·麥考伊（Rajiv McCoy）指出，儘管仍有許多工作要做，但該團隊的概念驗證——即證明新構想在實務上確實可行——非常成功。麥考伊本身的研究專注於妊娠流失，他解釋說，非整倍體是導致懷孕在出生前終止的主因。他表示，能夠減少這些錯誤的技術，可能會對人工受孕產業及整個社會產生巨大影響。由於約有一半的人類受孕在出生前就終止了，任何能幫助穩定這些細胞的方法，都可能改變許多家庭的生活。

paragraphs.en: Despite the excitement, the path to using this technology in humans is still long. The current study was limited to mouse eggs, and researchers must ensure that such a system is safe and effective for human use. Melina Schuh has spent the last two decades studying how egg cells work and why they change as they age. Her team’s work in 2015 first showed how the structures holding chromosomes together break down over time. Now, with the development of TALhesins, the scientific community has a new tool to potentially address these age-related changes.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管令人振奮，但將此技術應用於人類的道路依然漫長。目前的研究僅限於小鼠卵子，研究人員必須確保此系統對人類使用是安全且有效的。梅琳娜·舒過去二十年來一直致力於研究卵細胞的運作方式，以及它們為何會隨年齡增長而改變。她的團隊在二零一五年首次展示了將染色體結合在一起的結構如何隨時間瓦解。如今，隨著 TALhesins 的開發，科學界擁有了一項新工具，有望解決這些與年齡相關的變化。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the goal is to see if this system can eventually be developed into a treatment for humans. If successful, it could help expand the biological window for reproduction and provide new options for those struggling with infertility. While the researchers emphasize that there is still significant work ahead, the ability to stabilize chromosomes in aging eggs represents a major step forward. By addressing the root cause of chromosomal errors, scientists hope to reduce the rate of miscarriage and improve the chances of success for those seeking to have children later in life. The stakes are very high, as the ability to support healthy pregnancies remains a primary goal for reproductive medicine globally.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，目標是觀察此系統最終能否發展成人類的治療方法。如果成功，它將有助於延長生育的生理窗口，並為那些受不孕症困擾的人提供新選擇。雖然研究人員強調前方仍有重大工作，但穩定高齡卵子中染色體的能力代表了一大進步。透過解決染色體異常的根本原因，科學家希望降低流產率，並提高那些希望在較晚年齡生育的人們的成功機率。這項研究的利害關係極高，因為支持健康的懷孕過程，始終是全球生殖醫學的首要目標。

keyTerms.noteZh: 這是科技與研究領域的慣用語，指初步驗證想法是否可行。文中：the team’s proof of concept—a demonstration that a new idea can actually work in practice—was highly successful.

sources.name: STAT News
sources.title: In a fertility advance, engineered molecular glue stabilizes chromosomes in aging eggs

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the primary reason that human egg cells are particularly susceptible to chromosomal errors as a woman ages?

options.A: The body stops producing new egg cells after the age of 40.
options.B: The protein complex holding chromosomes together is not replaced over time.
options.C: The chromosomes in oocytes are naturally weaker than those in other body cells.
options.D: IVF procedures cause the molecular glue in egg cells to break down prematurely.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，女性體內的卵細胞（oocytes）自出生起就攜帶了所有遺傳物質，而負責連接染色體的蛋白質 cohesin（分子膠）在卵細胞中必須維持數十年且不會被替換，這導致了隨時間推移產生的錯誤。選項 A 雖然是事實，但不是導致錯誤的直接機制；選項 C 文中並未提及卵細胞染色體本身較弱；選項 D 則是因果倒置，IVF 是為了處理問題，而非導致問題的成因。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why is the success of TALhesins in mouse eggs considered a significant milestone for human reproductive medicine?

options.A: It proves that human infertility can be cured without further clinical trials.
options.B: It confirms that aneuploidy is the only factor contributing to pregnancy loss.
options.C: It demonstrates a potential method to correct the root cause of age-related chromosomal instability.
options.D: It shows that scientists have successfully extended the human biological clock by two decades.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第四段與第六段提到， aneuploidy 是導致懷孕失敗的主因，而 TALhesins 的成功證明了科學家能修復染色體連接，這解決了導致不孕的根本生理問題（root cause）。選項 A 錯誤，因為文中強調仍需漫長的臨床研究；選項 B 過度推論，文中僅說它是主因，未說它是唯一因素；選項 D 誇大了研究成果，目前僅在老鼠實驗成功，尚未應用於人類。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the author mean by the term 'proof of concept'?

options.A: A final product ready for public sale.
options.B: An initial demonstration that a theory can work in reality.
options.C: A complete medical cure for a specific disease.
options.D: A set of rules used to guide laboratory experiments.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章在第四段括號中明確定義了 'proof of concept' 為「a demonstration that a new idea can actually work in practice」（證明新想法在實務上可行）。選項 A 錯誤，因為該技術尚未進入人類臨床；選項 C 過於絕對，目前僅是實驗階段；選項 D 將其誤解為實驗流程規範，與文中定義不符。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article?

options.A: The global trend of delaying childbirth is causing a decline in the human population.
options.B: Researchers have found a way to completely reverse the aging process in women.
options.C: New scientific advancements are addressing the biological causes of age-related infertility.
options.D: IVF is no longer necessary because of new protein-based treatments for egg cells.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文核心在於討論女性因年齡增長導致的染色體錯誤（aneuploidy），以及科學家如何透過研發 TALhesins 等技術來嘗試解決此生理限制，以協助高齡生育。選項 A 雖在開頭提及，但非文章重點；選項 B 誇大了研究範圍，僅針對卵細胞而非全身老化；選項 D 錯誤，因為此技術是為了輔助 IVF 的成功率，而非取代 IVF。
